newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-BZW's Schmidt seeks bond business boost.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-BZW's Schmidt seeks bond business boost.

text.p: BZW's hiring of highly regarded German banker Roman Schmidt as global head of debt syndicate in London is another step in the bank's bid to boost its capability in the capital markets.
Schmidt -- well-known as Deutsche Bank's head of German capital markets after six years in Frankfurt -- is the latest appointment in a series of new positions at the bank.

Schmidt told Reuters in a telephone interview on Wednesday he was looking forward to the challenge of expanding BZW's Eurobond market syndicate operations from May 1. BZW is the investment banking arm of British bank Barclays.
"I've been watching BZW from the outside and they've made some very good hires in the investment banking area to move the new issues business forward," 34-year-old Schmidt said.
"The whole investment bank train of BZW is being put on the right track," he said.

Barclays' chief executive Martin Taylor, who has staked a lot in pushing BZW into the top league, has vigorously defended the large cash injection into the investment bank which posted a 29 percent fall in profits for 1996.
Schmidt said there was no reason why BZW should not be successful in non-sterling and dollar Eurobond transactions.

BZW has long been recognised for its prowess in its home market of sterling-denominated Eurobonds. So far this year it is top of the keenly-watched league tables for sterling bond issuance, with a solid market share of 15.5 percent.
But in the wider markets -- which so far this year has been dominated by Wall Sreet's big five including Merrill Lynch and Goldman Sachs -- it lags behind.
BZW is currently in 15th slot in international bonds in all currencies, according to Euromoney Bondware data, with a 2.6 percent market share.
At Deutsche Bank, Schmidt was responsible for German and eastern European origination as well as marks, French francs, guilders and Swiss franc debt syndication.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell's most recent benchmark transaction was a 2.0 billion mark seven-year deal for Russia, jointly lead by CSFB.
BZW's most recent ground-breaking transaction was a 1.25 billion stg June 2002 global bond jointly lead by Merrill Lynch.
Schmidt will report to Robert Morrice, co-head of European fixed income and head of European credit business.
"This is a key appointment in the development of our global markets capability," Morrice said in a statement on Tuesday.
"(Schmidt) has extensive expertise in the European capital markets and is respected by major borrowers worldwide."
Prior to Deutsche Bank Schmidt worked for CSFB in London.
Asked about London's status as a financial centre post European economic and monetary union, Schmidt said: "London is going to stay a major financial centre.
"After all, it was the birthplace of the Eurodollar market."
